top.titulo: China’s Diesel Exports Set to Plunge as Domestic Inventories Run Low
top.resumen_es: China’s diesel exports are on track to drop in November from the highs seen in August and September as increased fuel shipments at the end of the summer dented domestic inventories, traders and executives with knowledge of this month’s export plans told Reuters on Thursday. So far this month, Chinese refiners have sold about 500,000 metric tons of diesel for November loading, according to estimates by Reuters and trade sources. top.titulo: SOCAR Bets $1.65 Billion on U.S. Shale Gas Boom
top.resumen_es: Azerbaijan’s state oil and gas company SOCAR has struck a deal with Comstock to acquire some of its assets in the Haynesville shale and an infrastructure subsidiary. The price tag of the deal is $1.65 billion. top.titulo: Oil Prices Continue to Fall as Democratic Sweep Shakes Energy Markets
top.resumen_es: Crude oil prices moved even lower, and energy company stocks followed after the results of the U.S. midterms, as markets brace for a potentially radical change in U.S. policies. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $94.30 per barrel, after dropping by 9% on Wednesday, and West Texas Intermediate was trading at $87.35 per barrel, after shedding 8% on Wednesday, following the Democrats’ majority in both houses.
